title: sse: fix partial-json delimiter ordering and token/event framing for streaming responses
author: Priya Sharma
description: Background: multiple customers and internal e2e runs have surfaced a class of SSE streaming regressions when emitting partial JSON outputs via the OpenAI compatibility layer. Symptoms include (1) client SDKs receiving token events before the JSON delimiter sequence is emitted causing partial_json parsers to attempt to decode incomplete objects, (2) malformed SSE framing when events and delimiter tokens are interleaved across TCP frames, and (3) inconsistent ordering between token events and higher-level 'event' markers leading to SDK consumers interpreting tokens out-of-order. Reproducer: run the streaming structured-output example with long-generated JSON objects (depth > 2) and network chunking enabled (tests simulate 100-120 byte MTU). Motivation: streaming structured outputs must be stable for tool/function-calling and robust for consumers that rely on OpenAI-compatible partial-JSON delimiters. This PR fixes the underlying framing and ordering bugs and adds targeted tests. What I changed: - Introduced an explicit framing boundary buffer in src/runtime/sse/framing.rs to guarantee delimiter tokens ("\n\n" and the configured partial-json marker) are emitted atomically and not split across SSE frames. The buffer coalesces small writes and ensures event markers are flushed in a single SSE event when possible. - Reworked the token/event ordering in src/runtime/sse/streamer.rs: token bytes are now queued with sequence metadata and the event envelope is emitted only after the corresponding token payload has been written to the framing buffer. This prevents token events from being observed by the client before the delimiter sequence. - Added a minimal sequence-number prefix for internal ordering (not exposed to clients) to make stalls and reordering easier to debug in telemetry and to assist tests in asserting strict ordering. The prefix is stripped before sending to the wire. - Fixed OpenAI compatibility adapters (redwood-openai-compat/openai_stream_adapter.go) to respect the new framing semantics and to emit the "delimiter" event in the expected position for partial JSON implementations. - SDK updates: minor stabilization changes for Python and TypeScript streaming helpers to handle coalesced framing and to retry incremental parse on boundary conditions. - Tests: new integration test tests/integration/test_sse_streaming.py and unit tests under src/runtime/sse/tests that simulate MTU-level chunking and assert event/token ordering and valid partial JSON at all checkpoints. - Docs: updated docs/streaming.md with guidance for partial JSON consumers and recommended SDK parsing strategies. Compatibility and risk: The change preserves the external SSE protocol and OpenAI-compatible semantics; there is no breaking change for well-behaved clients. However, misbehaving clients that depended on the previous (buggy) interleaving may see different ordering - listed as low-risk. Rollout: squash-merged to main and cherry-picked to release/2026-02 for hotfix consumers. CI: unit + integration + e2e streaming ran and passed after a flaky integration test was re-run once. Notes for reviewers: pay attention to framing buffer boundaries and telemetry flags for sequence numbers. The implementation aims to minimize additional heap allocations and avoid adding per-token syscalls in the hot path.
commits: fix(sse): coalesce framing writes and ensure delimiter atomicity
fix(sse): enforce token->event ordering using temporary sequence buffer
chore(sdk): handle coalesced framing in python/typescript streaming helpers
test(sse): integration tests simulating small MTU and partial-json asserts
review_comments: Ethan Liu: Verified the integration test reproducer - ordering assertions now pass consistently. Please ensure telemetry sequence numbers are stripped from production payloads.
Author (Priya Sharma): Sequence numbers are scoped to runtime-debug builds and stripped by the final flush path. Added a flag 'sse.debug_sequence' to control this; default is false in prod.

Maria Gonzalez: Left a small nits about variable naming in framing.rs; suggested 'coalesce' -> 'coalesce_into_frame' for clarity. Also requested an additional comment on why we avoid per-token syscalls.
Author: Addressed naming nits and added comment explaining syscall avoidance; added a benchmark in perf-canary for comparison.

release_notes: Fix SSE streaming partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing. Improves streaming stability for structured outputs and OpenAI-compatible partial-JSON consumers. Includes tests and minor SDK adaptations.

Telemetry flag 'sse.debug_sequence' defaults to false in production
